Contributing to harnessr

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Bug reports, questions and pull requests are welcome at https://github.com/elkronos/harnessr/issues. For a bug, a short script that shows it with hr_mock_client() is the most useful thing you can send: it runs anywhere, with no key and no cost.

Working on harnessr

Running the tests

From the repository root:

bash run-tests.sh            # install what is missing, install the package, run the suite
bash run-tests.sh --check    # a full R CMD check instead
bash run-tests.sh --help     # the other options

The suite needs testthat and withr. Install future and future.apply too: without them, the tests of a parallel run’s call and cost counts are skipped. Every test runs offline: model calls go to a mock client, an R function or a local fake of the HTTP request, so no key is needed and no request leaves your machine. The parallel tests start worker processes, and each worker loads the installed harnessr, not your source tree. run-tests.sh installs the package first; when you run a test file yourself, reinstall with R CMD INSTALL . before it, or the workers run the old code. The tests workflow on GitHub runs the same suite, then runs the R blocks of the README, except those that install a package or need a PDF, a real key or ellmer, and compares the output each block documents with real output. It knits every guide with no key and no network, checks the registry counts the get started guide states against the registries, fails if two readers share a traversal signature, and fails if any of that left a new or changed file in the repository that git status reports. Files .gitignore names are not reported, so output that matches one of its patterns (docs/, *.Rout, sim-results/) passes that check unseen.

These scripts rewrite fixtures the tests compare against. Run them from the repository root, and only when you mean to change what they record:

Script What it rewrites
Rscript dev/record-golden.R the golden records in tests/testthat/fixtures/golden/ and fixtures/golden-heuristics/
Rscript dev/record-layers.R fixtures/boundary/layers.csv, the layer of every object in R/
Rscript dev/record-doc-internal.R fixtures/boundary/doc-uses-internal.csv, the core internals the document layer uses
Rscript dev/record-listings.R fixtures/registry/listings.rds, what each registry holds when the package loads
Rscript dev/build-stage-fixtures.R fixtures/stages/, one saved object of each review stage
Rscript dev/build-quote-fixture.R fixtures/quotes/, the labelled quotations the quote matchers are tested on
Rscript dev/build-pdf-fixtures.R fixtures/pdf/, the PDFs the PDF golden records read; needs pdftools
dev/record-legacy-keys.R fixtures/legacy-0.6.0/, a cache and a recording written by an old build; its header says how to rerun it with that build

Rscript dev/build-diagrams.R rewrites the four diagrams in man/figures/ from the code: the layers, a document run, composition, and the registry. Rerun it after changing a stage, a kind of module, a composition verb or a contract version, and commit the new SVGs. tests/testthat/test-diagrams.R fails until you do.

Rscript dev/ci/pr-checks.R <mode> origin/main HEAD runs a pull request check locally; the modes are tests, deps, lint, namespace, commits and dashes.

Checks on GitHub

A pull request runs these workflows:

Workflow Check names What it runs
R-CMD-check.yaml macos-latest (R release), ubuntu-latest (R release), ubuntu-latest (R oldrel-1) R CMD check with hard dependencies; a warning fails it
tests.yaml tests the suite with future, future.apply, ellmer and xml2 installed, from the source tree, then the README and guide checks described above
pr-checks.yaml pull request checks the tests, deps, namespace, commits and dashes modes, one step each; every step runs even when an earlier one fails, and the step name says which check failed
pr-lint.yaml lint changed R files the lint mode
pkgdown.yaml pkgdown builds the site without publishing it, only when the pull request changes a file the site is built from (the list is in the workflow)

Two more workflows never run on pull requests. ellmer-devel.yaml runs weekly and by hand: it installs ellmer from its GitHub repository and runs every test file that exercises hr_ellmer_client(). validation.yaml runs nightly and by hand: it simulates clustered benchmarks to check the coverage of hr_report()’s intervals (dev/sim-coverage.R) and checks hr_mdd() against a power simulation (dev/sim-power.R), 2000 replicates each, and keeps the tables as an artifact.

No workflow needs a repository secret. OPENAI_API_KEY is empty, or a dummy value for the README blocks, so a real key cannot change a result.

The dashes step fails when a pull request adds a line with an em dash, an en dash or a double hyphen between spaces. It reads R/, man/, vignettes/, inst/ (not inst/extdata/), dev/, .github/, the top-level Markdown files, DESCRIPTION and _pkgdown.yml, and leaves tests/ alone. It prints each line with its file and line number. Rewrite the sentence: split it, use a colon before an explanation or a list, or put a short aside in commas or parentheses. Prompt text sent to a model keeps its double hyphens, since changing it would change requests and cache keys; those lines are listed in tests/testthat/fixtures/boundary/dash-allowed.csv. The list also holds the name of the dashes step in .github/workflows/pr-checks.yaml, which quotes the mark it checks for. That list may only shrink, so a row added to it fails the tests step until the pull request carries the label tests-reviewed.

Adding or removing a label reruns pr-checks.yaml, so a label added after review turns its check green without a new push. Lint reads no label, so a label change does not rerun it; a push or a reopen does. A new push to a pull request cancels the older runs of the same workflow. On main, each merge gets its own run of R-CMD-check.yaml and tests.yaml, and pkgdown.yaml builds and publishes the site from the newest push to main. Only a run on main publishes: a release does not start pkgdown.yaml, and a run by hand on another branch builds the site without publishing it. Each publish replaces everything on gh-pages.

pr-checks.yaml used to run five checks: no weakened tests, no unreviewed dependencies, lint changed R files, no unreviewed export removals and no attribution in commit messages. Four of them are now steps of pull request checks, and lint changed R files comes from pr-lint.yaml. A branch rule or ruleset that requires the old names needs updating. Do not require pkgdown: a pull request that changes none of its files never starts it, and a required check that never starts stays pending.

What must stay true

  • Requests and cache keys do not move at the defaults. With every setting at its default, the package sends byte for byte the requests it sent before your change and computes the same cache and replay keys, so a cache someone has built and a recording they made keep working. A new setting is left out of a spec while it is at its default for this reason. The golden records check it.
  • The golden fixtures are the record of what the package does. test-golden.R and test-golden-heuristics.R compare every recipe, reader and review stage, the exported API, the numeral parser and the PDF layout pass with fixtures/golden/ and fixtures/golden-heuristics/. When a change in behaviour is intended, rerun dev/record-golden.R and say in the commit message what changed and why. Never rerun it to make a failure go away that you cannot explain.
  • The core does not reach into the document layer. Files named R/core-*.R are the general core; R/doc-*.R are the document layer. A core function may not call or read anything a document file defines, except the crossings in fixtures/boundary/allowed.csv. The document layer should use the core through its exports; the internals it still uses are listed in fixtures/boundary/doc-uses-internal.csv. Both lists may only shrink. test-boundary.R and test-doc-internal.R check this. Each exported core hr_ function needs a caller in the document layer or the tests, listed in NOTES-primitives.md. A change to what a module must do changes the contract version; see CONTRACT.md.
  • Results go outside the package. Tests, guides and help page examples write to tempdir() or a directory the user chose, never into the repository. Live runs and their results are kept outside the repository too.

What harnessr does not do

These keep the core small. A pull request that adds one of them will be asked to live in a separate package instead.

  • No domain types in the core: documents, chunks and pages belong to the document layer.
  • No sandboxing, file editing, patch application, git or process isolation. A user-written command step is allowed; the package never chooses, generates or isolates commands.
  • No multi-agent orchestration or debate, and no model choosing its own tools or skills. A person composes the steps.
  • No general workflow engine: stages run as a chain of hand-offs.
  • No model may register modules, or change evaluation sets, references, gates, budgets or ledgers.
  • No confidence from log probabilities, and no early stopping on them.
  • No model-controlled condensing or token-level prompt compression in the defaults.
  • No long-lived memory engine.
  • No new default that makes extra calls, samples, stages, judges or commands. A new module is opt-in until a benchmark shows it pays at the same cost.
  • No vector database and no set of provider SDKs: the built-in HTTP client, a backend function and the ellmer adapter are the transports.
  • No unvalidated model judge as the measure of accuracy or faithfulness.

Labels on pull requests

The pull request checks fail on some changes until a maintainer has reviewed them and added a label:

Label What it allows
tests-reviewed removing an expect_*() call, adding a skip(), or adding a row to allowed.csv, doc-uses-internal.csv or dash-allowed.csv
deps-reviewed adding a package to DESCRIPTION (it must be on CRAN either way)
exports-reviewed removing an export from NAMESPACE; list it under “## Removed” in NEWS.md with what to use instead

No label lets a commit message carry a Co-Authored-By trailer, a link to a chat or session, or a “Generated with” line. Reword the commit instead. This applies to commit messages only, not to the files.

When a test disagrees with your change

Report a conflicting test, never edit it to pass. A test that fails after your change is either a bug your change introduced or a test that encodes a decision your change reverses. Either way, say which test and why in the pull request, and let the review decide. Weakening a test, skipping it or rewriting its expected value to match new output hides exactly the change the test exists to show.
